newsitem.title: USA: Five firms to launch video CD players in India.
newsitem.headline: Five firms to launch video CD players in India.

text.p: C-Cube Microsystems Inc, a maker of semiconductors, said Friday that five electronics companies plan to launch video CD players using C-Cube chips in India, the leading movie-producing country in the world.

A video CD puts up to 74 minutes of VHS-quality video and CD-quality sound on a five-inch disk that closely resembles a computer CD-ROM. When attached to a television, a video CD player plays the disks much like a video cassette player.
C-Cube said Sony Corp, Philips Electronics NV, BPL Electronics Ltd, Thakral Holdings Ltd and DML as making players for India.
As many as nine companies will provide filmed entertainment on video CD.
Video CD players will also play audio CD.

"Video CD's low cost and robust media type is a terrific alternative to the VHS tape format, which is hampered by India's extreme heat and humidity," said Alex Daly, C-Cube vice president of marketing.
C-Cube shares rose 3-5/8 to 43-5/8 in mid-morning trading.
